key_insight: DEFEAT makes element identity and site occupancy differentiable, enabling joint gradient-based design of crystal composition, atom count, atomic positions, and lattice.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables targeted searches for superconductors and photovoltaic absorbers while incorporating an energy penalty to discourage unstable designs.
method: Extend a pretrained EquiformerV3 model to continuous species weights and site occupancies without fractional-data retraining.
Combine gradients from fine-tuned property models with a machine-learned energy penalty.
Validate candidates using first-principles calculations and assess finite-temperature stability with machine-learned potentials.
evidence_signal: DFPT yields Allen–Dynes critical temperatures above 10 K for 39 of 45 structurally novel designs; SCAN confirms ten novel absorber structures within 20% of a 1.34 eV target on raw or corrected gap scales, all within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull.
watch_item: Training-functional band-gap bias propagates into designs unless corrected in the objective, and finite-temperature phase competition can change static-hull rankings.
paper_title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
